passed: Real Windows High Contrast was enabled; matchMedia reported forced-colors: active and prefers-contrast: more.
SelectField foreground/background/border resolved to Windows CanvasText/Field system colors.
Native single-select, multiple listbox, disabled state and selected option semantics were exposed through Windows UI Automation.
The native select popup used the Windows Highlight/HighlightText palette.
Tab traversal moved from the source link to Department and then Priority.
The exact original Windows High Contrast state was restored and verified.

With High Contrast enabled before loading Edge, a real Tab action moved focus from the demo source link to Department; Windows UI Automation reported select-department focused=true and a visible orange focus outline was captured.
notCertified: No spoken Narrator, NVDA or VoiceOver output was audited. UI Automation tree inspection is not a substitute for a screen-reader acceptance run.
The new native High Contrast focus screenshot is visual-presence evidence; the focus outline RGB/contrast ratio was not separately sampled.

standardThemeFocusEvidence.limitation: Captured with High Contrast disabled; does not close the forced-colors focus indicator gate.

procedure: Start the standalone SSR host and verify its route returns HTTP 200 before enabling High Contrast.
Enable the actual Windows High Contrast White mode through SystemParametersInfoW; reload the demo in the dedicated Edge profile only after the OS mode is active.
Use Windows UI Automation to focus the View this runnable demo source link, press a real Tab key, then inspect the native control tree.
Capture the dedicated Edge window immediately after the focus transition.

visualEvidence.capture: Visible Edge window captured immediately after Tab while native Windows High Contrast White was active.
visualEvidence.observed: A visible orange focus outline is rendered around the Department native select. The screenshot is retained in this evidence directory.
visualEvidence.pixelContrastMeasurement: Not separately sampled; this is visual presence evidence, not a numeric contrast-ratio claim.
